config.title: Missed Parcel in Berlin - FAQ
config.subtitle: Where a missed parcel goes in Berlin, how long each carrier keeps it, and what to bring when you collect it.

items.q: How long does DHL keep a missed parcel in Berlin?
items.a: In a DHL branch or partner shop, **7 working days**, with Saturdays counted and Sundays and holidays not. In a Packstation, **usually 7 calendar days**, weekends and holidays included. After that it goes back to the sender.

items.q: How long does Hermes keep a parcel in a PaketShop?
items.a: **7 working days**, starting on the day the parcel reaches the shop. Hermes says the period cannot be extended. Older guides that still say 10 days are out of date.

items.q: How long does a DPD or GLS parcel wait?
items.a: DPD keeps a parcel **7 calendar days in a Pickup shop and only 3 calendar days in a DPD locker**. GLS keeps it **8 working days** from the day after it arrives at the ParcelShop.

items.q: What ID do I need to collect a parcel in Berlin?
items.a: Bring **ID with your name on it**. Hermes accepts an EU, EEA or Swiss ID card, a passport, a German residence permit or a travel document, but **not a driving licence or a health insurance card**. A DHL Packstation opens with the code in the Post & DHL app.

items.q: Can someone else pick up my parcel?
items.a: Yes, with a **signed authorisation (Vollmacht)** and their own ID. Hermes has a printable form, and DHL prints an authorisation field on the back of its card.

items.q: Do Berlin public holidays give me more time?
items.a: Only on the **working-day clocks** of DHL shops, Hermes and GLS. Lockers count every day. 31 October is a normal working day in Berlin, unlike in Brandenburg, so it does not add a day.

items.q: How do I stop missing parcels?
items.a: Set a **named neighbour, a safe place or a Packstation or PaketShop** as your delivery choice with each carrier, and switch on tracking emails so the clock never starts without you knowing.
